What would be your advice for anyone starting college soon?
pick subject(s) you like have lots of sex party hard but dont forget to actually study
I agree. Orangesn0w listen to this guy/girl!

Decide why you're there and keep that in mind when making decisions. What degree are you doing?

I can't speak for US colleges (never lived there), but I've done a number of university (undergrad and postgrad) degrees in Australia. What I can say is that certain fields are very competitive (e.g. science) whereas others have a tonne of jobs waiting (e.g. engineering). If you're in a competitive field, you need to study your arse off and graduate near the top of your class if you want a pathway into a good job; if it's a less competitive field you can afford to relax a lot more. Whatever you do in life (study or party or whatever) you will end up making sacrifices. Just make sure those sacrifices are things you are comfortable with.
Go go class. It's easy to skip, I know. You're paying a lot of money to go so you might as well go. It can only help you.
Make sure that you are going because it actually will help you with your career goals and not just going cause "it's the next thing to do."

Get up and go to class. If you don't have classes go to the library and study until 5 or 6pm anyway, after that time unless you are in a crunch period do whatever you want. Sport? Cool. Videogames? Great. Get to know people and join at least two clubs or societies, it will help to stand out within each of them to be "that guy from Club B" instead of "the new guy". Be friendly and ready to change your mind about a lot of things. Final note: university is not for everyone, if you feel unhappy is ok to quit sooner than later.

GO TO CLASS! Try and do your homework on time, even if it isn't graded.Take all of your liberal arts classes (History, English, humanites, etc) online, you don't waste any time in a boring lecture, you don't have to study for tests depending on the school (some have the tests online instead of in a testing center), and they're less work (according to my friends who made the mistake of taking them as lecture classes).

REMEMBER TO ACTUALLY TALK TO OR EVEN ASK OUT THAT HOT GIRL/GUY IN YOUR CLASS!

It's been more than a couple of decades, but some things stay the same.

First, don't do what I did. I dropped out of college. Although my life is, by any standard, a success, I had to work three times as hard at it because I didn't have that degree. There were even many drams I had where I wasn't even able to get my foot in the door because of it. So, stick with it.

Next, beware of distractions. College life is an incredible time where you're free to make choices...including bad choices. I know that the person you met at a party last night wants you to drop some acid and attend an orgy tonight, but if you have an exam the next morning, take a rain check. Your school work has to come first.

On the other hand, embrace those distractions as well. It's a time of change. The minute you set foot on the campus, everything about you starts new. If you have baggage, it's because you stupidly brought it with you. Decide who you want to be, and live it. Hang out with people you had never imagined hanging out with. Explore ideas that you never thought of before. Embrace the change.

Finally, remember that the key to a happy life is paying your debts. Whoever is paying for you to be there expects something in return. Don't fail them by squandering your opportunity.

Try to get any general ed classes out of the way as soon as you can. I knew too many people who put something off until the end, and were scrambling around their last semester trying to fulfill some bullshit requirement so that they could graduate.

Don't be too discouraged if you get partway through your first semester and realize that you actually have no idea how to properly study. It happens to a lot of people because high school is crap for that sort of thing. Don't be too proud to ask for help.

If you have a few spare elective classes to fill up, don't just take something easy. Take something that you find interesting, even if it is a bit harder.

If you're in a dorm (halls for English) get a door stop and when you arrive and unpack prop it open. It makes you accessible and you'll make friends easier. Also focus on friends for your first year instead of relationships, they'll last longer. Final advice would be to read your notes at the end of the day, even if just a quick scan. You'll remember much more that way. Have fun!
You can slack in high school and still get good grades. College is not like that. Apply yourself!
Live in the dorms. Keep your door open all the time. Say yes to every opportunity.
